title: "Comping rhythm: Long notes"
subtitle: "For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
---

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Long notes**. It is one of the first patterns to learn, so this page starts from it and takes it into the band. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad*, *Boogaloo*, *Bossa nova*, *Tango*, *Piano ballad*, *Boom-chick*, *Straight-eighth rock*, *Reggaeton*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop*, *12/8 doo-wop*, *Hymn (four parts)*, *Folk carol*, *Emo / pop-punk* and *John Prine Fingerpicking*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Long notes, slowly

**How to play it.** One chord, struck once, held for the bar. On piano, play it and keep the keys down (or the pedal down) until the chord changes; on guitar, strum once and let it ring. Use it to learn the chords and the changes before any rhythm.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 72 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C G|Am F|Dm G|C" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## In other styles

The same comping rhythm in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.
